source.title: A Comprehensive Evaluation of LLM Unlearning Robustness under Multi-Turn Interaction

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether apparent forgetting persists under a different set of recovery probes: corrective prompts, dialogue histories, and few-shot examples. It does not test the listed fine-tuning, activation-ablation, or quantization attacks.
record.gate_note: The study reports results for self-correction, dialogue-conditioned querying, and few-shot conditioning. The cited recovery and relearning results from other papers are background only and are not recorded as rows. Learning-rate sweeps are described and shown in figures, but their values are figure-only; they are not included in the rows below.
record.test_reason: The study tests whether WMDP-Bio knowledge removed by GA, NPO and RMU (Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Zephyr-7B-Beta) comes back under prompting alone. The prompts are self-correction feedback, five-turn dialogue histories and five-shot context. It reports WMDP and MMLU accuracy against single-turn baselines, so its results bear on A and E. It uses no fine-tuning, ablation or quantization.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that static single-turn evaluation may overestimate forgetting. GA/NPO knowledge comes back under corrective feedback and dialogue context, and even unrelated MCQ histories trigger partial recovery. RMU and stronger unlearning (higher learning rate) resist recovery, but the authors attribute this to behavioural rigidity and lost responsiveness, not real erasure. RMU's utility also collapses once forget-set content appears in context.
record.recipe_differences: Uses GA, NPO, and RMU unlearning checkpoints, but evaluates them with custom self-correction, multi-turn dialogue, and few-shot protocols rather than reproducing the original studies' robustness recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery varies with unlearning method and context. The authors report stronger effects for structurally aligned histories and further amplification from semantic relevance in some settings; RMU is comparatively resistant. The figure-based learning-rate sweeps are not extracted as rows.
record.problems: Only two instruction-tuned models are tested, and evaluation is limited to multiple-choice questions and particular prompting templates, as the authors note. No uncertainty estimates are reported in the tables. Extracted results do not establish recovery to the original model's performance; many increases are partial, and RMU often does not recover.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row limit, omitted Table 1 self-correction results for methods other than Llama–GA and Llama–NPO, and omitted the remaining Table 4 WMDP-Cyber self-correction results. Also omitted WMDP-Cyber dialogue and few-shot results (Tables 5 and 8), MMLU utility rows (Tables 3, 6, 9, and 10), and the additional few-shot context conditions in Tables 7 and 8. The learning-rate ablations in Figures 2–9 are figure-only and not extracted.

untested.parts: Resistance to fine-tuning, internal-edit, quantization, jailbreak, paraphrase and other-language attacks; only self-correction, dialogue-history and few-shot prompting were tried.
Not tested; no activation ablation or representation analysis. The 'shallow suppression' and 'behavioural rigidity' readings are argued from behaviour only.
Paraphrasing, jailbreaks, other languages and open-ended generation; only multiple-choice evaluation with logit-based option selection was used.
Not tested; no new robust method is proposed or evaluated.

missing.what: MMLU utility of the unlearned checkpoints. GA/NPO score 23.00-29.97 vs 57.36 (Llama) and 55.24 (Zephyr). RMU scores 55.22/54.28 but falls to 22.95/25.32 with WMDP content in context. A's 'keeps general ability' verdicts rest on these numbers. rows_left_out declares them, but no row carries them.

Self-correction results for RMU and the other GA/NPO variants, which the RMU and E verdicts partly rest on. Llama-RMU: R1 26.87, S1 31.89, S2 53.81 (CondAcc 36.84 vs 33 chance). Zephyr-RMU: S1 39.75, S2 55.77. Zephyr-NPO: S1 54.28. Zephyr-GA: S1 71.56.

record.verdict_notes:
What changed from the previous verdict:
(1) The two list-valued row_fixes items were split into one item per row: the 14 single-turn rows (R01, R04, R07, R10, R13, R16, R19, R22, R25, R28, R31, R34, R37, R40) are linked to A only and observed, and R02 and R03 are absent. Each single-turn item now gives that checkpoint's MMLU from Table 3.
(2) New fix for R21: partial changed to absent. The authors call RMU's change 'minimal', and the E-challenges label already treated the row as flat.
(3) The E limits_scope label was split into two condition groups: partial recovery for most GA/NPO variants, and little or no gain for Llama-GA and Zephyr-NPO (R02, R03, R32, R33, R43, R53). Both of those checkpoints still recover under feedback.
(4) The A-challenges reason no longer cites the range R05-R18, which included single-turn rows.
(5) The A limits_scope label now also cites R49 and R56: MMLU collapses under few-shot WMDP context too (Table 9).
(6) Table 1 RMU self-correction (text) was added to the RMU A-supports and E-challenges reasons.
(7) Two missing entries were dropped: Table 4 WMDP-Cyber self-correction and the Figures 2-9 learning-rate sweeps. rows_left_out declares both and no verdict rests on them. The figures show stronger unlearning lowering recovery while ΔAns goes to zero.
Everything else is kept.

Reading notes:
- For attack rows linked to both A and E, the state describes recovery, which is E's effect. Observed recovery counts against A's claim that simple attacks don't recover the knowledge.
- The GA/NPO checkpoints collapse general ability (MMLU near chance), so they are weak tests of hidden knowledge. Their WMDP gains under dialogue and few-shot context come with MMLU gains, which may reflect format or behaviour repair rather than recovery of the specific knowledge.
- The RMU checkpoints are public releases (Li et al. 2024a and 2024b).
- The S1/S2 baselines in the record use Round-1 accuracy; chance-adjusted baselines are about 40-50%.
- The paper reports no uncertainty.
- The record's A-challenges label cites a claim about 'a model that never saw the knowledge', which version A does not contain.
- The roughly 1,273-item size of WMDP-Bio, used to convert small gains into item counts, comes from the WMDP benchmark, not this paper. The values are consistent with it.
- No instructions to the reader were found in the text.

versions.untested_parts: The study evaluates target accuracy after unlearning, recovery under interaction, and utility on MMLU, but the extracted rows focus on recovery results rather than MMLU utility.
No fine-tuning or relearning training set is applied; few-shot conditioning is evaluated separately.
No activation-direction ablation or internal representation analysis is performed.
Tests corrective prompts, dialogue histories, and five-shot ground-truth conditioning. Does not test paraphrasing, jailbreaks, or other languages.
No newer counter-method designed to resist these attacks is tested.

relationships.condition: GA/NPO variants (with and without GD/KL regularization), both models, WMDP-Bio
relationships.reason: These checkpoints fail A before any attack: MMLU is 23.00-29.97 vs 57.36/55.24 for the originals (Table 3, from the text; no row). Prompting also recovers WMDP-Bio: strongly under feedback (R57, R58, R60) and introspection (R59), and by 4-10 points after WMDP dialogue (R05, R08, R11, R14, R17, R23, R26, R29, R35, R38).
relationships.display_finding: MMLU fell to 23.00–29.97 versus original 57.36 and 55.24, while feedback and introspection recovered WMDP-Bio knowledge and WMDP dialogue added 4–10 accuracy points.

relationships.condition: RMU checkpoints (public releases, both models): WMDP-Bio accuracy under dialogue, few-shot and self-correction prompting
relationships.reason: WMDP-Bio is near chance (R19 27.18, R40 30.95) and MMLU is kept (55.22/54.28 vs 57.36/55.24, Table 3, text). Dialogue and few-shot leave accuracy flat or lower (R20, R21, R41, R42, R49, R56). Table 1 self-correction stays near chance-adjusted levels (text).
relationships.display_finding: WMDP-Bio accuracy was 27.18 and 30.95, with MMLU at 55.22/54.28 versus 57.36/55.24; dialogue and few-shot prompting left accuracy unchanged or lower, and self-correction remained near chance-adjusted levels.

relationships.condition: RMU general ability once WMDP forget-set content is in the context (dialogue or few-shot)
relationships.reason: From the text (Tables 3, 9; no row): RMU MMLU falls from 55.22 to 22.95 (Llama) and from 54.28 to about 25.3 (Zephyr) with WMDP context. RMU also barely revises answers (S1 ΔAns 17.62 vs 99.76 for the base); the authors read this as rigidity, not erasure. Rows: R20, R41, R49, R56.
relationships.display_finding: MMLU fell from 55.22 to 22.95 on Llama and 54.28 to about 25.3 on Zephyr, while answer revision measured 17.62 versus 99.76 for the base.

relationships.condition: Llama-GA and Llama-NPO under explicit corrective feedback (S1/S2) and introspective reconsideration (S3)
relationships.reason: Round-2 accuracy is well above chance-adjusted baselines: R57 59.23 (vs about 40), R58 75.65 (vs 50), R60 69.68 (vs about 50). S3 raises it from 24.98 to 41.48 with only 17.75% of answers changed (R59). Table 1 shows the same for the other GA/NPO variants (text).
relationships.display_finding: Second-round accuracy reaches 59.23, 75.65 and 69.68 against chance-adjusted baselines of about 40, 50 and 50 respectively; introspective reconsideration raises accuracy from 24.98 to 41.48 while changing only 17.75% of answers.

relationships.condition: GA/NPO variants other than Llama-GA and Zephyr-NPO, under five-turn dialogue histories (target or unrelated MCQ) and five-shot WMDP context
relationships.reason: Recovery is partial: gains of 1-13 points (mostly 4-13), to 26-38% vs 62-67% for the original models (R05-R55 listed). The same contexts also raise MMLU for these collapsed checkpoints (Table 3, e.g. Zephyr-GA 23.85 to 30.56, text), so part of the gain may be format repair.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy gained 1–13 points to reach 26–38%, versus 62–67% originally; Zephyr-GA MMLU also rose from 23.85 to 30.56, suggesting some gains may reflect format repair.

relationships.condition: Llama-GA and Zephyr-NPO under dialogue histories and five-shot context
relationships.reason: Little or no gain: R02 +0.47, R03 +0.39, R32 +0.31, R33 -0.08, R43 +2.20, R53 +1.41. Yet both checkpoints recover strongly under corrective feedback (R58 75.65; Zephyr-NPO S1 54.28 in Table 1, text), so recovery depends on the kind of prompt.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy changes ranged from −0.08 to +2.20 points, although corrective feedback reached 75.65 for Llama-GA and 54.28 for Zephyr-NPO.

relationships.condition: RMU checkpoints (both models) under dialogue histories and five-shot context
relationships.reason: Accuracy falls or stays flat: R20 27.18 to 24.67, R41 30.95 to 25.29, R49 24.67, R56 26.16, R42 29.93, R21 +1.41. Table 1 S1/S2 stay near chance-adjusted levels (text). The authors attribute this to rigidity, not erasure.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy fell from 27.18 to 24.67 and from 30.95 to 25.29, with another gain of only 1.41; the authors attributed the weak response to rigidity rather than erasure.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Self-correction and dialogue-conditioned prompting for the extracted GA/NPO rows
reader_labels.reason: Target accuracy rises substantially after interaction, contrary to the claim that simple attacks recover no more than on a model that never saw the knowledge; see R05–R18, R23–R39, and R57–R60.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Some RMU and Zephyr–NPO dialogue results show no increase or a decrease, so recovery is not uniform across methods and conditions; see R20–R21, R33, R41–R42, R49, and R56.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Explicit corrective feedback, target-related dialogue, and five-shot WMDP-Bio examples for GA/NPO methods
reader_labels.reason: These prompting and context conditions raise WMDP accuracy above the single-turn reference; see R05–R18, R23–R39, R43–R48, R50–R55, and R57–R60.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Several RMU outcomes decline or remain unchanged, and Zephyr–NPO has little or no gain in some dialogue settings; see R20–R21, R33, R41–R42, R49, and R56.
